To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

timeout from avoidance is an effective control variable for the sequential reacquisitions of rats, that the duration of this variable affects the rate at which the sequence is completed, and the shock density of the task.

(1) timeout from avoidance is a controlling variable in sequential reacquisition; (2) timeout duration affects both rate of sequence completion, and shock density, and; (3) timeout duration does not affect the percentage of errors.
the rate of sequential reacquiring is a function of timeout duration from avoidance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of various manipulations of the timeout from avoidance procedure on the reacquisition of a sequence of three responses.
the analysis of the effects of timeout from avoidance on the reacquisition of a sequential response sequence.
the effects of timeout duration on sequential reacquisition.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the timeout variable is a controlling variable, and that the timeout variable has a significant effect upon the sequential reacquisitional performance of a group of animals, and that the effect is a function of the magnitude of the timeout variable.
sequential reacquisition of three-member sequences is controlled by a combination of timeout duration and shock density.

the effects of timeout from avoidance on the sequential re-acquisition baseline are similar to those of food, and that these effects are similar to those obtained with other schedules of food presentation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
timeout duration has differential effects on rate and density of responding, but not on the accuracy of responding, in a sequential reacquisition task.
the sequential reacquistion baseline is controlled by the interaction of timeout and shock density.
the reacquisition of a sequence is controlled by a combination of the timeout from avoidance and the shock density.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the timeout from avoidance is a powerful variable for controlling behavior, and that the timeout duration can be manipulated to control the rate of sequence completion.
timeout from avoidance, a variable that has been largely ignored in the learning literature, is a potent reinforcer.
timeout duration affects rate of sequential reacquisitions and shock densities.
